subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
passage:
Observation note, Saturday preparedness session, community hall.
Sangeeta, about fifteen, came with her parents and her grandmother. Near the end her father said, “If the phone networks fail, we all meet here at the community hall. If someone can't get here, we each try to reach Masi in another city.” Sangeeta copied four key numbers in ink onto paper, then made three copies: one for her school bag, one for her mother's purse, one for beside the fridge. She asked me what happens if the hall is locked. I told her the porch stays open, and she wrote that down as well. Her grandmother asked her to read the numbers back, and Sangeeta did it twice without hurrying. I've invited her to show the paper card to the next group.
— Yogesh, volunteer

qa.q: Where will the family meet if the phone networks fail?
qa.a: They will all meet at the community hall.

qa.q: What does Sangeeta's question about a locked hall suggest she is thinking?
qa.a: It suggests she is a little worried about what could go wrong and wants the plan to hold up, so she checks the details carefully.

qa.q: What could the family add to the plan, and why?
qa.a: They could agree on a time to check in at the hall each day, so nobody waits without knowing whether the others are safe.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta's grandmother see the plan?
qa.a: Her grandmother probably feels reassured, since she knows where to go and whom to reach without a phone, and she checks that Sangeeta can read the numbers back.

grounding: A family agrees a meeting place and an out-of-town contact in case networks fail, and the teen writes key numbers on paper.

subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
passage:
Sunday
Family meeting after dinner, because of the flood warnings. Papa asked, “If the phones stop working, how do we find each other?” Nobody had an answer. I realised all our numbers live only inside our phones. If my battery dies, I don't even know Mummy's number by heart.
So we decided:
1. If the networks fail and we're apart, everyone goes to the community hall near the water tank. We wait there.
2. Everyone contacts Mausi in Pune, because a far-away line may work when local ones are jammed. She becomes our message centre.
3. I write the important numbers on paper.
Damini Didi said paper is old-fashioned. I said paper doesn't run out of battery. She laughed and agreed.
I've made four small cards: Papa, Mummy, Didi, Mausi and the hall address. One in each school bag, one in Papa's wallet, one on the fridge.
– Mridul

qa.q: Where will the family meet if the networks fail?
qa.a: At the community hall near the water tank.

qa.q: What worried Mridul when Papa asked the question?
qa.a: Mridul felt uneasy realising all their numbers lived only in phones, and not even Mummy's number was known by heart.

qa.q: What else could the family do to make the plan work?
qa.a: Practise it once, each person saying the plan aloud, and learn at least one number by heart.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Damini Didi?
qa.a: Damini Didi teases that paper is old-fashioned, then laughs and agrees, seeing it can't run out of battery.

grounding: Shows a family agreeing to meet at the community hall and contact one relative in another city if networks fail, with the teen writing key numbers on paper.

subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
passage:
Family group: Tenzin, Pala, Amala, Madhav (Delhi)
Tenzin: after today's landslide warning, can we make a plan? if phones stop working here, what do we do
Pala: good question
Tenzin: idea: if we can't reach each other, everyone goes to the monastery community hall and waits there
Amala: yes, it's on high ground
Tenzin: and we choose one person outside Gangtok. local lines jam but a far call can still work
Tenzin: Madhav, can you be our contact person?
Madhav: of course. i'll keep my phone on loud. whoever reaches me, i pass the message on
Tenzin: i'm writing all our numbers + Madhav's + the hall on paper cards, one for each bag
Pala: put one in the car too
Tenzin: done. 5 cards
Amala: proud of you 🙏

qa.q: Where does Tenzin suggest everyone go if they can't reach each other?
qa.a: The monastery community hall, and wait there.

qa.q: What might Tenzin have been worried about after the landslide warning?
qa.a: Tenzin was worried the family could be separated with phones down and no way to find each other.

qa.q: What else could the family add to the plan?
qa.a: Agree how long to wait at the hall before moving on, and walk the route there once so everyone knows it.

qa.q: How might Madhav feel being chosen as the contact?
qa.a: Madhav likely feels trusted and responsible, keeping the phone on loud so any message can be passed on.

grounding: Shows a teen proposing that the family meet at a community hall and use one relative in another city as contact if networks fail, and writing numbers on paper.
